notes: Standalone example: lists who can administer the endpoint as text. The built-in sensor resolves SIDs and object classes on Windows and reads sudoers on Linux; this example only lists group membership, so sudoers-only grants and uid 0 accounts other than root are not shown.

commands.linux:
# Standalone example: members of the sudo, wheel and admin groups, as text.
# The built-in sensor also reads /etc/sudoers and sudoers.d and reports uid 0 accounts.
getent group sudo wheel admin 2>/dev/null | awk -F: '$4 != "" { n = split($4, m, ","); for (i = 1; i <= n; i++) print m[i] " (" $1 " group)" }'
echo "root (uid 0)"
commands.darwin:
# Standalone example: members of the admin group, as text.
dscl . -read /Groups/admin GroupMembership | sed 's/^GroupMembership: //' | tr ' ' '\n'
commands.windows:
# Standalone example: members of the local Administrators group, as text.
# The built-in sensor also reports each member's SID, object class and whether it is local or from the domain,
# and falls back to net localgroup on a domain controller.
$ErrorActionPreference = "Stop"
try { Get-LocalGroupMember -SID 'S-1-5-32-544' | ForEach-Object { $_.Name } } catch { net localgroup Administrators | Select-Object -Skip 6 | Where-Object { $_ -and $_ -notmatch 'command completed' } }
